issues.legal_issue: Rent-control protection can become applicable when a building reaches the statutory age threshold while an eviction proceeding is pending.
material_facts: The building was deemed completed on the date its first tax assessment took effect.
The eviction suit was filed before the building reached ten years of age, but it reached that age while the litigation was pending.
The tenant sought protection under the rent-control Act.
issues.conclusion: The Act became applicable when the building reached ten years of age during the litigation. The tenant was entitled to seek its protection, subject to meeting the applicable statutory conditions, and the case was remanded to allow those matters to be determined.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(2) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, provides an exemption for the first ten years from the building’s deemed completion date. Once that period expires during litigation, the Act applies; Sections 20, 39 and 40 indicate the protections and conditions available to the tenant. Om Prakash Gupta v. Dig Vijendrapal Gupta was distinguished because the building in that case had not reached ten years during the relevant proceedings.

predicates.eviction_suit_pending: A landlord has brought an eviction suit against a tenant and the proceeding remains unresolved.
predicates.building_age_threshold_reached_during_li: The building reaches the age at which the applicable rent-control regime begins to govern it while the proceeding is pending.
predicates.tenant_seeks_rent_control_protection: The tenant asks to receive the protections available under the rent-control regime.

issues.definition: When an eviction suit remains pending, the building reaches the relevant age during the litigation, and the tenant seeks rent-control protection, the tenant may claim that protection.

issues.legal_issue: A court may take account of a subsequent event that materially affects relief while litigation is pending, provided fairness to both sides is preserved.
material_facts: The building reached the age threshold for rent-control protection after the eviction suit was filed but before the litigation concluded.
The tenant brought the building’s changed status and the resulting claim for protection to the court’s attention.
The case was remanded so the parties could address the amounts due and the tenant could meet the conditions for protection.
issues.conclusion: The court could and should take account of the building reaching the relevant age during the litigation, subject to scrupulous fairness to both sides.
issues.legal_principle: In Pasupati Venkateswarlu v. Motor and General Traders, the Court held that a court may, and in appropriate cases must, take cautious account of events after a proceeding begins when they fundamentally affect the right to relief or how relief should be moulded, provided fairness to both sides is observed. The Court applied that principle here.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding_pending and subsequent_event_materially_affects_relief and subsequent_event_brought_to_court and fairness_to_both_sides_preserved

predicates.eviction_proceeding_pending: A court proceeding concerning eviction remains unresolved.
predicates.subsequent_event_materially_affects_reli: An event after the proceeding began changes the parties’ entitlement to relief or how that relief should be shaped.
predicates.subsequent_event_brought_to_court: A party brings the later event to the court’s attention while the proceeding is pending.
predicates.fairness_to_both_sides_preserved: The court gives both sides a fair opportunity to address the later event and its consequences.

issues.definition: If an eviction proceeding remains pending and a party brings to court a later event that materially affects relief, the court may consider it when fairness to both sides is preserved.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment that adds facts supporting an existing basis for relief or defence, without introducing a new claim on a new factual basis, does not introduce a new cause of action.
material_facts: The tenant sought only the protection of the rent-control Act, which became applicable to the building during the litigation.
The Act contemplated necessary amendments to the pleadings and the taking of additional evidence where required.
The court held that seeking this protection did not change the cause of action.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s request for the Act’s protection did not create a new cause of action, and necessary amendments to the pleadings and additional evidence could be allowed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied A.K. Gupta & Sons v. Damodar Valley Corporation: an amendment that merely adds to facts already on the record, without making a new claim on a new factual basis, does not introduce a new cause of action and may be allowed even after the limitation period. Section 39 of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, also contemplates necessary amendments and additional evidence.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_pending: A court proceeding concerning eviction remains unresolved.
predicates.amendment_adds_supporting_facts: A party seeks to add facts that support a claim or defence already raised in the proceeding.
predicates.amendment_introduces_no_new_claim_basis: The proposed amendment does not assert a new claim founded on a new factual basis.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is pending and an amendment adds supporting facts without introducing a new claim basis, the amendment may be allowed.
